summary: Wilde reported to Reginald Turner that Hylton had arrived in Paris 'with his boy Herbert'.

sources.quote: Hylton is here with his boy Herbert. I must say he is almost impossible. He is a sort of grown-up man with a hysterical womb, and makes scenes with Sir John like a woman with child.
sources.context: Wilde to Reginald Turner, Tuesday [postmark 6 December 1898], Hôtel d'Alsace, Paris (MS Hyde). The 'he' who is almost impossible is Hylton, not Herbert. The folio is A census of the paris exile household in December 1898 and form one: Sir John Ashton and his 'little friend' Joseph (both already on this map, connected on this same page), Turner's 'little friend' Alphonse, and Hylton with 'his boy' Herbert. Four young men in three sentences, all described to Wilde's closest correspondent in the same possessive formula.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the record for Herbert.

manuscript.repository: British Library, London (Lady Eccles Oscar Wilde Collection)
